groups.text: An authorization makes three remote calls.
It looks up the card, in forty ms, and scores the fraud risk, in sixty.
Then it sends both to the issuer, whose client returns a CompletableFuture.
Each call hands you a future, a box that gets its value later.
You attach the next step to a future, and you pick the method by the shape of that step.
thenApply takes a plain function, from one value to another: here, from the issuer's response to a decision.
It returns a new future at once.
When the response arrives, the function runs on it, and the new future gets the decision.
If you know Optional or streams: thenApply is map.
Now the next step is the issuer call.
authorize does not return a response.
It returns a future of one.
Attach it with thenApply, and the new future holds whatever authorize returns: another future.
The outer one completes as soon as authorize returns.
The answer arrives later, in the inner one, and no one waits for it.
A declared result type makes the compiler catch this.
Without one, it compiles.
thenCompose is for this shape.
It takes the future the function returns, and hands you one flat future that completes when that one does.
When the issuer answers, it completes.
thenCompose is flatMap.
thenCombine waits for two futures.
The card lookup and the fraud score don't depend on each other.
Both calls started on their own lines, with supplyAsync, before anything was attached.
So they run side by side.
The card is back at forty.
The fraud score at sixty.
Then thenCombine calls your function with both values.
The slow part takes sixty ms, the longer of the two.
The speed comes from starting both futures early, not from thenCombine.
Start the fraud call inside thenCompose instead, and it begins only when the card is back.
That takes one hundred ms, and nothing warns you.
Put together, the authorization is three lines.
Kotlin calls the same Java A P I.
Only the lambda syntax changes.
Pick by the shape of the step.
Two futures and a function of both: thenCombine.
A step that returns a future: thenCompose.
Plain code on one value: thenApply.
